stages.name: Your stories
stages.line: Turning what you wrote into facts you can approve.

stages.name: Your goals
stages.line: Turning what you want into directions and limits.

stages.name: Companies
stages.line: Sorting and filling in the companies a search finds.

stages.name: Roles
stages.line: Deciding which roles deserve your time.

aiSteps.name: Read a story
aiSteps.starts: You choose Read on a story.

reads.text: The story being read
Your roles and facts
Roles and facts already waiting in Review, so it doesn’t repeat them
Your other stories, for background only
Your directions and limits
Facts you rejected, with your reasons

aiSteps.may: Propose roles, facts and context, each with the words it came from.
aiSteps.mayNot: Take a fact from any story but this one, or invent a customer, number, result or skill.

aiSteps.name: Read the changes
aiSteps.starts: You choose Read on a story that was read before.

reads.text: The version it read before, and the new one
Your other stories, for background only
Your roles and facts
This story’s facts, approved or waiting
Facts you rejected, with your reasons

aiSteps.may: Propose new facts and updates to facts the change affects, and flag facts the story no longer says.
aiSteps.mayNot: Touch facts from other stories, or change an approved fact without your okay.

aiSteps.name: Rewrite a fact
aiSteps.starts: You choose Add context or rewrite on a fact.

reads.text: The fact, its history and its role’s context
The story the fact came from

aiSteps.may: Suggest new wording, with your note as the final word.
aiSteps.mayNot: Replace the fact. The new wording waits for you to accept it.

aiSteps.name: Follow-up questions
aiSteps.starts: You choose Suggest questions on Review.

reads.text: Your record
Your stories, for background only
Questions already asked, answered or set aside
Your projects and their facts

aiSteps.may: Ask a few short questions where an answer would add or change a resume line.
aiSteps.mayNot: Ask again what you set aside.

aiSteps.name: Check for disagreements
aiSteps.starts: You choose Check for disagreements on Record, or Look for conflicts on Review.

reads.text: Your roles and facts, and answers you’ve given
Every story

aiSteps.may: Ask which version is right when a story and your record disagree.
aiSteps.mayNot: Pick one for you.

aiSteps.name: Insights
aiSteps.starts: After a story or project is fully reviewed, and when you choose Find new insights.

reads.text: Your roles, facts, context and directions
Your stories, for background only
Insights you approved, still to review or rejected, so it doesn’t repeat them
Your projects and their facts

aiSteps.may: Propose what’s true of you across roles and projects, each citing approved facts.
aiSteps.mayNot: Bring back an insight you rejected, or cite a fact you haven’t approved.

aiSteps.name: Gather skills
aiSteps.starts: You choose Gather on Skills.

reads.text: The skills and tools of your roles
The stack and languages of your projects
Your facts
Skills, tools and certifications you approved or that are waiting in Review
Skills you rejected, with your reasons

aiSteps.may: Propose each skill, tool and certification once, with where your record shows it, and offer near-duplicates as merges.
aiSteps.mayNot: Bring back a skill you rejected, in any spelling, or change one you approved beyond adding where it shows.

aiSteps.name: Find duplicates
aiSteps.starts: You choose Find duplicates on Record, or Find facts said twice on Review.

reads.text: Facts you approved or that are waiting in Review, by role, and the pairs you kept apart

aiSteps.may: Flag facts in the same role that say the same thing, for you to merge or keep both.
aiSteps.mayNot: Merge anything itself, or flag a pair you kept apart.

aiSteps.name: Find same work
aiSteps.starts: You choose Find same work on Record, or you link a project to a role.

reads.text: The project: its name, summary and stack, and the role it’s linked to
That role’s title, employer and dates
The facts of the project and of its role not yet connected, and the pairs you kept apart

aiSteps.may: Suggest pairs of a project’s facts and its role’s facts that describe the same work.
aiSteps.mayNot: Connect facts without you, or pair facts you kept separate.

aiSteps.name: Read a project
aiSteps.starts: You choose GitHub repositories to read on Projects, or Read again on a project.

reads.text: The repository: its files, history and languages
This project’s facts, approved or waiting, so it doesn’t repeat them
This project’s facts you rejected, with your reasons
Your directions, for what matters to you

aiSteps.may: Propose the project and facts about it, each citing the files it came from.
aiSteps.mayNot: Fetch anything that looks secret, like .env files, keys or certificates. It can open that one repository and nothing else.

aiSteps.name: Read my goals
aiSteps.starts: You choose Read my goals.

reads.text: Your goals story
Your roles and facts
Your directions and limits, kept as they are
Directions and limits you rejected

aiSteps.may: Propose directions, and limits as clear values you can check and correct.
aiSteps.mayNot: Assume a limit you didn’t state. It leaves out anything it would have to guess.

aiSteps.name: Filters from wording
aiSteps.starts: You edit a limit’s wording.

reads.text: That limit’s wording, and nothing else

aiSteps.may: Set the limit’s filters to match what it now says.
aiSteps.mayNot: Read your goals story for it.

aiSteps.name: Directions and search criteria
aiSteps.starts: You choose Fill in or Suggest more on Goals.

reads.text: Your record, insights, limits and directions
Your stories, for background only
Directions you rejected or haven’t reviewed yet, so it doesn’t repeat them
Your projects and their facts

aiSteps.may: Fill in each direction’s positioning, target titles, the market’s words for the work, which stories carry over, and its search criteria. Suggest new directions.
aiSteps.mayNot: Overwrite anything you approved.

aiSteps.name: Screen companies
aiSteps.starts: After each company search.

reads.text: Each company’s name and website

aiSteps.may: Sort companies into places to work and non-employers: recruiters, job boards, associations, government, schools, media and investors.
aiSteps.mayNot: Delete anything. You can restore a company it set aside.

aiSteps.name: Fill in companies
aiSteps.starts: After a company search, or when you choose Fill in details, Check again or Check all again.

reads.text: The company’s website
Your directions and limits
Companies you turned down, and why, as preferences

aiSteps.may: Add what each company builds, its size and its fit, and find its job board.
aiSteps.mayNot: Spend Apollo credits past the credits you set aside each month.

aiSteps.name: Sort roles
aiSteps.starts: Once the descriptions of newly found roles are all in.

reads.text: Your directions: their names, positioning and titles
Each role’s title
Each role’s description, without what its company repeats in every posting
The company’s name

aiSteps.may: Decide which of your directions a role could be for, leaning toward including it.
aiSteps.mayNot: Judge how well it fits. That’s the next step.

aiSteps.name: Rank roles
aiSteps.starts: Right after sorting.

reads.text: Your projects and their facts
Your directions and limits
Each role, and the directions the sort passed it to
Each role’s whole description, without what its company repeats in every posting
The company’s name and one-line summary
Your roles and their facts, and your years of work
Whether to count how big a stretch a role is
Roles you turned down, and why, as preferences, never as limits

aiSteps.may: Rate the role for each direction as strong, some, weak or none, with a score from 0 to 100 and a reason in plain words.
aiSteps.mayNot: Predict whether you’ll be hired. The score says how much of your time the role deserves.

aiSteps.name: Resume
aiSteps.starts: You choose Write, Write again, Add what’s new or Update all on Resumes, Write the resume or Rewrite on Goals, or Tailor a resume on a direction or a role.

reads.text: Your skills, tools and certifications
Your roles, facts, insights and context
Your career breaks, with the reason in your words
The length to write to
The direction’s positioning, for a direction or tailored resume
For a tailored resume, the direction resume it starts from
Your projects and their facts
Facts that describe the same work, as one
For a tailored resume, the role’s title and place
For a tailored resume, the role’s company
For a tailored resume, the role’s description

aiSteps.may: Write a base resume, one for each direction and one tailored to a role, each line citing approved facts, with how well you cover each requirement: strong, partial or thin.
aiSteps.mayNot: Cite anything you haven’t approved. A line with no approved fact behind it is marked No approved basis.

aiSteps.name: Cover letter
aiSteps.starts: You choose Write a cover letter in a pursuit.

reads.text: Your record: roles, facts, projects, context, insights, skills and directions
The resume tailored to the role, or the one you sent
The pursuit: its role, company, direction and what you sent
The role’s place
The role’s description
The company’s summary
Your name, to sign it

aiSteps.may: Write a first-person letter whose paragraphs cite approved facts. Your edits become a new version.
aiSteps.mayNot: Write one before a resume is tailored to the role, or once the pursuit was sent.

aiSteps.name: Ask about this role
aiSteps.starts: You ask a question in a pursuit.

reads.text: Your record: roles, facts, projects, context, insights, skills and directions
The conversation so far and your latest message
The resume tailored to the role, or the one you sent
The pursuit: its role, company and what you sent
The role’s place
The role’s description
The company’s summary

aiSteps.may: Answer application questions in the first person, ready to paste, and say when your record doesn’t support something.
aiSteps.mayNot: Claim what your record doesn’t support. Anything new you tell it comes back as proposals to review.

aiSteps.name: Outreach
aiSteps.starts: You choose Draft a message for a person in a pursuit.

reads.text: Your record: roles, facts, projects, context, insights, skills and directions
Who it’s to: their name, title, group and whether they’re likely the hiring manager; who else you already wrote to there
The pursuit: its role, company and when you applied
The role’s description
The company’s summary
Your name, to sign it

aiSteps.may: Draft a short outreach message signed with your name: who you are, why this role, why you fit, and one small ask, for you to send from your own email.
aiSteps.mayNot: Send anything. You send it, then mark it sent.

aiSteps.name: Follow-ups
aiSteps.starts: A follow-up is due after a quiet application or an interview, and you choose Write the follow-up in its pursuit or Write follow-up on Today.

reads.text: Your record: roles, facts, projects, context, insights, skills and directions
Where your application stands: its status, dates and timeline
Follow-ups you already sent
Who it’s to, and what you already sent them
The role’s description
Your name, to sign it

aiSteps.may: Draft a short follow-up email signed with your name, for you to send from your own email.
aiSteps.mayNot: Send anything. You send it, then mark it sent.

aiSteps.name: Check against facts
aiSteps.starts: You choose Check against facts on a resume line you put in your own words.

reads.text: The facts the line rests on (for the summary, the facts the whole resume rests on)
Your words, and where the line sits

aiSteps.may: Say whether your words say only what their facts support, and which words go beyond them.
aiSteps.mayNot: Change your words. It only answers.

aiSteps.name: Update lines
aiSteps.starts: You choose Update lines on a document whose facts changed since it was written.

reads.text: The facts the lines cite, as they read now and as they read when the lines were written
A rejected fact a line cites, as what to take out
The resume in use: its lines, your own words and what it was written from
The newest version of a letter not yet sent
A pursuit’s answers, and whether it was sent (a sent one is left alone)

aiSteps.may: Rewrite just the lines that cite a changed fact.
aiSteps.mayNot: Change a document until you choose Apply.

aiSteps.name: Compare models
aiSteps.starts: You choose Compare in Settings, AI.

reads.text: One story, without your record

aiSteps.may: Run one of three tasks (reading a story, the base resume or insights) on up to four models, for you to judge.
aiSteps.mayNot: Add anything to your record.

aiSteps.name: Test call
aiSteps.starts: You choose Try it in Settings, AI.
aiSteps.may: Send one test prompt to check your key and model work.
aiSteps.mayNot: Read or change your record.

actions.label: Bring your data from another copy
actions.detail: Opens Settings, Your data, to import an export from another CareerBot copy.

actions.label: Start
actions.detail: Starts a pursuit of this role: its status, resume, letter, answers and people in one place.

actions.label: Connect Google Drive
actions.detail: Opens Google to let CareerBot keep a Google Doc of each resume in a CareerBot folder in your Drive. You come back here once it’s done.

actions.label: Skip
actions.detail: Leaves Google Drive out of Getting started. Connect it any time in Settings, Google Drive.

actions.label: Save and continue
actions.detail: Checks the key with OpenRouter, then saves it with your budget and model. You can change any of them in Settings.

actions.label: Save and continue
actions.detail: Checks the key with Apollo and reads the credits left in your plan, then saves it with your credit budget and how Apollo work runs. You can change any of them in Settings.

actions.label: Open
actions.detail: Opens the pursuit, with what’s next.

actions.label: Open
actions.detail: Opens the pursuit, to answer the offer.

actions.label: Open
actions.detail: Opens the new version, to keep or discard it.

actions.label: Open
actions.detail: Opens it with the lines resting on changed facts, to update them.

actions.label: Open
actions.detail: Opens the follow-up, to read and send it.

actions.label: Review
actions.detail: Opens Review, where each decision waits in the order it unlocks your other work.

actions.label: People
actions.detail: Opens the pursuit’s contacts, to write to the next one.

actions.label: Close · No response
actions.detail: Closes the pursuit as No response.

actions.label: Open in Pursuits
actions.detail: Opens the pursuit, with its resume, letter, answers and people.

actions.label: Discard
actions.detail: Deletes the new version; the current one stays.
actions.note: Free · Asks first · can’t be undone

actions.label: Keep
actions.detail: Makes the new version the one you use.

actions.label: Rewrite
actions.detail: Writes a new version from your approved record, for you to keep or discard.

actions.label: Suggest questions
actions.detail: Looks for questions whose answers would sharpen your record. They wait here for your answers.

actions.label: Look for conflicts
actions.detail: Checks your record against your stories for anything they disagree on. What it finds waits here.

actions.label: Find facts said twice
actions.detail: Looks for facts your record says twice. Pairs it finds wait here, to merge or keep both.

actions.label: Open Today
actions.detail: Opens Today: what needs you now.

actions.label: Skip for now
actions.detail: Moves on to the next one; this one keeps waiting.

actions.label: Copy
actions.detail: Copies the answer, to paste into the application.

actions.label: Edit
actions.detail: Change the question or the answer.

actions.label: Remove
actions.detail: Removes this answer from the pursuit.
actions.note: Free · Asks first · can’t be undone

actions.label: Keep
actions.detail: Saves this answer to the pursuit's Answers.

actions.label: Copy
actions.detail: Copies the answer.

actions.label: Copy and open Mail
actions.detail: Copies the follow-up and opens it in your email, addressed and ready to send.

actions.label: Keep the new one
actions.detail: Keeps the new version as your draft.

actions.label: Keep the one I had
actions.detail: Drops the new version; your draft stays as it was.

actions.label: Edit
actions.detail: Change the words yourself.

actions.label: Copy
actions.detail: Copies the letter as it was sent.

actions.label: Copy
actions.detail: Copies the letter.

actions.label: Edit
actions.detail: Change the words yourself; it's kept as a new version.

actions.label: People
actions.detail: Shows your contacts, to write to the next one.

actions.label: Close · No response
actions.detail: Closes the pursuit as No response.

actions.label: Change
actions.detail: Write your own next step; clear it to go back to the suggested one.

actions.label: Add
actions.detail: Adds them to this pursuit’s contacts.

actions.label: Mark a reply
actions.detail: Records that this person answered. Moves the pursuit to In conversation if it’s behind.

actions.label: Clear the reply
actions.detail: Takes back that this person answered.

actions.label: Copy and open Mail
actions.detail: Copies the message and opens it in your email, addressed and ready to send.

actions.label: Download resume
actions.detail: Downloads this pursuit’s tailored resume as a PDF to attach to your email.

actions.label: Mark as sent
actions.detail: Keeps the message as sent, on the pursuit's timeline.

actions.label: By direction
actions.detail: Shows how your pursuits went for each direction, and where roles come from.

actions.label: Copy link
actions.detail: Copies a link that opens this role in Pursuits.

actions.label: Start
actions.detail: Starts a pursuit of this role: its status, resume, letter, answers and people in one place.

actions.label: Companies you’d name
actions.detail: Lists companies you already want, added to every search.

actions.label: Seed companies
actions.detail: Lists companies you’d love to work at, so searches find ones like them.

actions.label: Lens settings
actions.detail: Sets how your goals shape searches and what Found shows.

actions.label: Let it be set aside
actions.detail: Moves it back to Doesn’t fit your goals.

actions.label: Edit website and job board
actions.detail: Opens its website or job board for editing.

actions.label: Open its website
actions.detail: Opens the company’s site in a new tab.

actions.label: Open its roles in Pursuits
actions.detail: Shows its open roles in Pursuits.

actions.label: Open Found
actions.detail: Shows the companies found for you.

actions.label: Start outreach
actions.detail: Starts a pursuit at this company without an open role, to write to the people who hire there.

actions.label: Connect Google Drive again
actions.detail: Google stopped accepting CareerBot, so this resume isn’t kept in Drive now. Opens Settings to connect it again.

actions.label: Edit
actions.detail: Puts this line in your own words on this resume. It stays built on the same facts, marked Edited.

actions.label: Hide
actions.detail: Leaves it out of this resume. It stays here, struck, to bring back.

actions.label: Edit
actions.detail: Puts the summary in your own words on this resume. A new version is written with its own summary.

actions.label: Use CareerBot’s
actions.detail: Puts CareerBot’s summary back.

actions.label: Show
actions.detail: Shows it on this resume again.

actions.label: Undo
actions.detail: Brings the line back, to add or skip.

actions.label: Add
actions.detail: Adds this line to the resume. The rest stays as it is.

actions.label: Skip
actions.detail: Leaves it off. What it’s built on isn’t proposed again for this resume unless you change it.

actions.label: Save
actions.detail: Saves your words on this resume. Its PDF, Word and Google Doc follow.

actions.label: Download PDF
actions.detail: Saves this resume as shown, as a PDF.

actions.label: Download Word
actions.detail: Saves this resume as shown, as a Word file.

actions.label: Copy for Google Docs
actions.detail: Copies the resume with its headings and bullets, to paste into Google Docs or Word.

actions.label: Copy plain text
actions.detail: Copies the resume as plain text.

actions.label: Download plain text
actions.detail: Saves the resume to a file, as plain text.

actions.label: Restore
actions.detail: Makes a copy of this version the current one.

actions.label: Compare with current
actions.detail: Shows this version beside the current one, with what changed.

actions.label: Don’t fold
actions.detail: Shows this role on its own again.

actions.label: Leave this role out
actions.detail: Takes this role off. It stays listed here, to show again.

actions.label: Show this role
actions.detail: Puts this role back on.

actions.label: Type a title
actions.detail: Opens a field to write the title yourself.

actions.label: Save
actions.detail: Shows the role under the title you typed.
actions.note: Free · Change it from the same menu

actions.label: Compare versions
actions.detail: Shows two versions side by side, with what changed.

actions.label: Compare
actions.detail: Shows the new version beside this one, with what changed.

actions.label: Open the pursuit
actions.detail: Opens the pursuit for this posting.

actions.label: Resumes to update
actions.detail: Shows the resumes your record has changed under, or with a new version waiting.

actions.label: Save
actions.detail: Saves the break to your record, approved as you gave it.

actions.label: Edit
actions.detail: Changes its months or its reason.

actions.label: Add a fact
actions.detail: Adds a fact about this break to your record.

actions.label: Add a note
actions.detail: Adds a dated note to this break.

actions.label: Undo approval
actions.detail: Takes the break back to review, so resumes stop using it.

actions.label: Approve
actions.detail: Puts the break back in your record, so resumes use it.

actions.label: Restore
actions.detail: Puts the break back in your record, approved.

actions.label: Remove
actions.detail: Takes the break out of your record and every resume, with why if you like.

actions.label: Copy link
actions.detail: Copies a link to this break.

actions.label: Open
actions.detail: Opens the break.

actions.label: Add as a career break
actions.detail: Starts a break with these months filled in.

actions.label: Copy the insight
actions.detail: Copies the insight’s words.

actions.label: Save
actions.detail: Keeps the insight in your wording, approved.

actions.label: Open Review
actions.detail: Opens the insights waiting for you to approve or reject.

actions.label: Keep
actions.detail: Leaves GitHub connected.

actions.label: Change the reason
actions.detail: Changes why you rejected it.

actions.label: Add a fact
actions.detail: Adds a fact about this project to your record.

actions.label: Undo approval
actions.detail: Takes the project out of your record and back to review.

actions.label: Save and approve
actions.detail: Saves your corrections and approves the project.

actions.label: Add a fact
actions.detail: Adds a fact to this role in your words, approved as you write it.

actions.label: Add context
actions.detail: Adds your own context to this role, to sharpen its facts.

actions.label: Add a break before this role
actions.detail: Starts a break with the months between this role and the one before.

actions.label: Copy link
actions.detail: Copies a link to this role.

actions.label: Undo approval
actions.detail: Takes the role back to review; resumes stop using it.

actions.label: Delete role…
actions.detail: Deletes the role with its facts, context and notes.
actions.note: Free · Asks first · can’t be undone

actions.label: Both are right
actions.detail: You held both jobs at once. Neither changes, and this isn’t asked again.

actions.label: Record is right
actions.detail: Keeps your record as it is. This question isn’t asked again.

actions.label: Story is right
actions.detail: Changes your record to what the story says.

actions.label: Neither
actions.detail: Type what’s right; your record takes it.

actions.label: Open story
actions.detail: Opens the story this was read from.

actions.label: Save
actions.detail: Changes your record to what you typed.

actions.label: Save
actions.detail: Keeps this with the role; rewrites of its facts use it.

actions.label: Add context
actions.detail: Adds something true about this role in your words; rewrites of its facts use it.

actions.label: Change why
actions.detail: Changes why you rejected it.

actions.label: Edit
actions.detail: Your wording, approved as you write it.

actions.label: Offer again
actions.detail: Offers the two as the same thing again, to merge or keep both.

actions.label: Goals story
actions.detail: Opens your goals story, which lives in Goals.

actions.label: Save
actions.detail: Saves what you wrote as a new version.
actions.note: Free · Earlier versions stay in Versions

actions.label: Edit direction
actions.detail: Change its title, what it includes, its fit and what it is.

actions.label: Edit positioning
actions.detail: Change the positioning, the titles to aim at and the words to use. Saving approves it.

actions.label: Undo approval
actions.detail: Moves it back to Proposed; roles aren’t ranked for it until you approve it again.

actions.label: Undo positioning approval
actions.detail: Puts the positioning back up for review; resumes aren’t written from it until you approve it again.

actions.label: Undo criteria approval
actions.detail: Puts the criteria back up for review; search doesn’t look for them until you approve them again.

actions.label: Add criteria
actions.detail: Write what search looks for in this direction. Saving approves them.

actions.label: Edit positioning
actions.detail: Change the positioning, target titles and vocabulary. Saving approves them.

actions.label: Restore
actions.detail: Puts it back among the proposed directions.

actions.label: Write your goals
actions.detail: Opens your goals story to write in. Reading it later proposes your limits and directions.

actions.label: Edit the story
actions.detail: Change your goals story. Saving keeps it as a new version.

actions.label: Limits
actions.detail: Opens the limits read from your goals and the ones you added.

actions.label: Directions
actions.detail: Opens the kinds of work you’re going for.

actions.label: Back to the current version
actions.detail: Shows the story as it reads now.

actions.label: Undo approval
actions.detail: Puts it back with the proposed limits; nothing filters by it until you approve it again.

actions.label: Open in Review
actions.detail: Opens Review, where it waits with what else is proposed.

actions.label: Delete
actions.detail: Deletes this limit you added; nothing filters by it after.
actions.note: Free · Asks first · can’t be undone

actions.label: Edit
actions.detail: Change it before approving; saving approves it.

actions.label: Keep the rule
actions.detail: Keeps filtering by the rule as it is, and stops asking.

actions.label: Your goals story
actions.detail: Opens your goals story, where proposed limits are read from.

actions.label: Proposed limits in Review
actions.detail: Opens Review, where proposed limits wait for you to approve or reject them.

actions.label: Roles in Pursuits
actions.detail: Opens every role in Pursuits, to see what your limits hide and rank lower.

actions.label: Sign out
actions.detail: Signs you out on this device and clears anything you were writing here that isn’t saved.
actions.note: Free · Sign in again to come back

actions.label: Change password
actions.detail: Asks for your current password, then a new one. Your other devices are signed out.

actions.label: Change password
actions.detail: Saves your new password. Your other devices are signed out.

actions.label: Add a person
actions.detail: Adds an account to this copy, with a workspace of its own. You choose the username; you get a temporary password to give them.

actions.label: Copy
actions.detail: Copies the temporary password.

actions.label: Add a person
actions.detail: Adds an account to this copy, with a workspace of its own. You get a temporary password to give them.

actions.label: Use the main model
actions.detail: Goes back to the model every other task uses.

actions.label: What the model sent back
actions.detail: Shows the start of the reply the model sent back.

actions.label: Disconnect
actions.detail: Stops syncing and ends CareerBot’s access to your Drive. Your CareerBot folder and its Docs stay in Drive.
actions.note: Free · Asks first · Connect again any time

actions.label: Choose a folder
actions.detail: Opens Google’s folder picker to choose where the CareerBot folder lives. It moves there with everything in it.

actions.label: Export
actions.detail: Makes one .zip of everything in this workspace, ready to download. Nothing here changes.

actions.label: Download
actions.detail: Saves the .zip to this device.

actions.label: Export again
actions.detail: Makes a new .zip of everything as it is now.

actions.label: Choose another file
actions.detail: Puts this file aside, to choose a different export.

actions.label: Continue
actions.detail: Picks the import up where it stopped.

configuration.name: CAREERBOT_VERSION
configuration.text: Which CareerBot release to run. Unset: the release this compose.yaml came with. A version such as 0.8.0 stays on it until you change it here; `latest` moves to the newest release on each `docker compose pull`. Before changing it, back up and read the release notes: https://careerbot.dev/changelog

configuration.name: SITE_URL
configuration.text: Where people open CareerBot, as the browser sees it. On your own computer: http://localhost:3000. On a server with a domain: its https address (https://careerbot.example.com), with your proxy or tunnel sending it to WEB_PORT.

configuration.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL
configuration.text: A) Convex's cloud (free plan). Create a project at https://dashboard.convex.dev, then: NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL: Settings > URL & Deploy Key, the deployment URL (https://….convex.cloud) CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY: Settings > URL & Deploy Key, Generate Production Deploy Key CONVEX_SITE_ORIGIN isn't needed: Google and GitHub send people back to https://….convex.site. Uncomment the two lines below and comment out or delete B's four lines.

configuration.name: CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY
configuration.text: A) Convex's cloud (free plan). Uncomment the two lines below and comment out or delete B's four lines.

configuration.name: COMPOSE_PROFILES
configuration.text: B) Self-hosted Convex, run by this compose file on this computer. Its data stays in the convex-data Docker volume. On a server with a domain, NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL and CONVEX_SITE_ORIGIN are two https addresses of their own (https://convex.example.com, https://convex-site.example.com) that your proxy sends to CONVEX_PORT and CONVEX_SITE_PORT. CONVEX_SELF_HOSTED_URL stays as it is: the setup step reaches Convex inside compose.

configuration.name: SIGNUP_ALLOWLIST
configuration.text: People sign in with a username and password: the owner's account is made with the setup code, and the owner adds everyone else in Settings, Account. Google and GitHub are optional; the sign-in screen offers them once they're set. Who may sign in with Google or GitHub: their emails, comma-separated. Empty: nobody (password accounts don't need it). Changing the list takes effect after `docker compose up -d`; to empty it again, delete SIGNUP_ALLOWLIST in the Convex dashboard's environment variables (an empty value here leaves the one there as it is).

configuration.name: AUTH_GOOGLE_ID
configuration.text: Each of Google and GitHub needs an OAuth app whose callback URL is your Convex HTTP actions URL plus /api/auth/callback/google (or /github): self-hosted on this computer: http://localhost:3211/api/auth/callback/google self-hosted on a server: CONVEX_SITE_ORIGIN/api/auth/callback/google (https://convex-site.example.com/…) Convex's cloud: https://your-deployment.convex.site/api/auth/callback/google Google: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials (OAuth client ID, Web application) GitHub: https://github.com/settings/developers (New OAuth App; its homepage URL is SITE_URL)

configuration.name: JWT_PRIVATE_KEY
configuration.group: Made for you the first time
configuration.text: Left empty, the first `docker compose up` makes these and keeps them in your Convex deployment's settings. Set them only to bring keys from another copy. MASTER_KEY_V1 encrypts the API keys people save in CareerBot; losing it means entering those again.

configuration.text: Choosing a Google Drive folder in Settings (a browser API key for Google's Picker).

configuration.name: LIQUIDAI_API_KEY
configuration.text: Liquid AI's model, for an experiment in sorting roles.

configuration.name: UPDATE_CHECK
configuration.text: Once a day this copy asks https://careerbot.dev/releases.json whether there's a newer version, and its owner sees it in Settings, Updates. Nothing about you or this copy is sent, but like any web request it shows careerbot.dev this server's IP address. off: never ask (the owner can also turn it off there).

configuration.name: WEB_PORT
configuration.text: Ports on this computer, if the defaults are taken. Change SITE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL and CONVEX_SITE_ORIGIN to match when they're localhost addresses (behind a domain they stay as they are). Dokploy's own dashboard is on 3000: there, set WEB_PORT=3001 or another free port.

configuration.name: BIND_ADDRESS
configuration.text: The address those ports are published on. 127.0.0.1 (the default): this machine only; Coolify's and Dokploy's proxies don't need them, and on a server they'd skip the proxy and its HTTPS (Docker's ports also go around ufw). Set 0.0.0.0 only to reach the ports from other machines without a proxy, never on a server facing the internet.
